body:
## Problem
`review_schedules.start_due` starts each due schedule's review. When `start` fails (no reviewer model, another review already open, a store error), it only runs `eprintln!("scheduled system review {id}: …")` and moves the schedule on.

The desktop app's human never sees stderr. The review silently doesn't happen, and nothing records it: no missed notice and no past entry. The comment says "is not retried", so the human only finds out by noticing that no findings arrived.

## Change
In `start_due`, when `start(&kinds)` returns `Err`:
- Record it on that schedule the same way a missed review is recorded: set `missed` to the due time and `missed_read` to `false`.
- Add a `reason` field with the refusal's message.

The existing missed-review banner (`sysreview.missed_notice`, also shown on Delivery) then offers **Run now** and **Skip**. Extend `sysreview.MissedReview` / `missed_decoder` with an optional `reason`. Extend `sysreview.missed_text` to read e.g. "Weekly security review was due <time> and couldn't start: <reason>." when a reason is present.

## Check
- Add a Rust test in `review_schedules` tests: call `start_due` with a `start` closure that returns `Err(Failure("E7003 …"))`. Check that the schedule now lists as missed, unread, with that reason.
- Add a Gleam test in `test/schedule_test.gleam` or `sysreview_test.gleam`: `missed_text` with a reason includes it.
- Keep the existing missed-review tests passing.
title: Tell the human when a scheduled review can't start
